title: Learning Unbiased Permutations via Flow Matching
claim: Iterative or integrator-based methods leave constraint violations that decay or grow, while ours holds the constraint exactly at every step.
layout: 1 panel, line plot, left-to-right, color-coded curves with inline labels
description: A single schematic line plot. The y-axis is row/column-sum violation and the x-axis is iteration or time t. A blue solid curve starts high and decays toward zero, labeled as Sinkhorn's residual going to 0 as the iteration converges. A red dashed curve rises exponentially, labeled as a manifold ODE error bound proportional to e^{Lt}. A thick dark-green line with dots at each Euler step lies flat on the x-axis inside a light-green band. It is labeled PermFlow (ours): 0 at every Euler step, with an arrow pointing up to it. The color-coded text labels sit next to their curves. The eye goes first to the green baseline and the contrast with the other two curves.
caption: Row/column-sum violation. With finitely many normalisation steps, Sinkhorn typically leaves a residual, which vanishes as the iteration converges; for integrators on general manifolds without projection, standard error bounds contain a factor eLt (dashed: a bound, not necessarily the realised violation). With the projected velocity, every Euler step of PermFlow preserves the linear constraints.
abstract: Learning permutations is fundamental to sorting, ranking, and matching, but existing differentiable methods based on entropy-regularized Sinkhorn produce a single softened solution and collapse under ambiguity. We present PermFlow, a conditional flow matching framework that operates directly on the affine subspace of matrices with unit row and column sums. A closed-form tangent-space projector preserves these constraints exactly along every trajectory, by construction rather than through iterative correction, and a nearest-target coupling routes distinct noisy initializations toward distinct valid permutations. The result is a model that captures multimodal permutation distributions rather than collapsing them to a single mode. On a range of problems, PermFlow achieves high accuracy on unambiguous inputs and recovers both valid permutations under ambiguity.
